page: Amazon Web Services hpc7g.16xlarge is an ARM64-based high-performance computing server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor architecture running at 2.6 GHz. The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 97889.61 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20607.0. Memory performance is a key strength, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3157.08 and uncached read memory bandwidth of 276.16 GB/sec. Software compilation using Clang is highly efficient, registering a top-tier Geekbench score of 59046.0. However, single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1533.0, and LLM text generation on small models is relatively weak at 57.23 tokens/sec.

Given its dedicated physical cores, high memory bandwidth, and 200 Gbps network baseline, the hpc7g.16xlarge offers high resource density and cost efficiency for parallelized, memory-bound compute workloads. The lack of local storage requires external storage integration, which is a tradeoff for data-heavy local processing. This server is optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) workloads, software compilation, database operations, parallelized scientific simulations, and static web serving.
